schools.name: Brown
schools.one: Compare aid and your credit plan before you choose the optional binding plan.
facts: The 90-second video is an optional introduction.
Feb 15 is a complete-file timing marker, not an early deadline.
schools.next: Confirm aid and the optional binding plan. Ask how aid works without GI Bill benefits. Share an essay outline once it is ready for useful feedback.

fin.waiver: No application fee for veterans, who use the separate Veterans Application.
fin.model: Veterans are admitted need-blind. General transfer admission is need-aware. Brown meets full demonstrated need.
fin.aid: Veterans submit the FAFSA, a prior-year tax return and a VA Certificate of Eligibility. Veteran aid materials were due March 1 in the 2026 cycle, so recheck 2027. On your call: VR&E pays out like a Post-9/11 GI Bill.
fin.vet: Service to School VetLink partner with an unlimited undergraduate Yellow Ribbon program for eligible students.
fin.note: The binding rolling option means you withdraw other applications if admitted. Compare aid first.

schools.abroad: Brown students in good standing can study abroad for a semester or year in sophomore, junior or senior year, after declaring a concentration. Brown aid can apply if aid requirements are met and a Consortium Agreement is filed for non-Brown programs. Courses need pre-approval to earn credit. No rule specific to transfer or veteran-route entrants was found: ask Brown study abroad advising.

schools.name: Cornell ILR
schools.one: Get ILR to review your course titles, descriptions and grades, and confirm sophomore or junior entry.
facts: ILR says most admitted transfers have a 3.4+ college average.
Cornell as a whole admitted 9.3% of Fall 2024 transfer applicants. That is not an ILR rate.
schools.next: Map writing, economics, math and science courses with ILR. Choose next courses for ILR readiness and your real direction.

fin.waiver: No transfer fee-waiver rule was found. Ask ILR admissions.
fin.model: ILR says transfer aid follows the same need-based policies as first-year students. Whether domestic transfer admission is need-blind was not confirmed.
fin.aid: ILR admits transfers for fall only, with a March 15 application deadline. The CSS Profile transfer deadline was March 15 in the 2026 cycle.
fin.vet: Yellow Ribbon participant with a Veterans Summer Bridge and a veteran admissions pathway that can waive some documents.

schools.abroad: ILR says transfer students are eligible to apply for semester study abroad and ILR credit internship programs (Ireland, England, Australia). The usual rules: full-time, junior or senior year, good standing and the ILR core finished. Aid transfers for Office of Global Learning programs and is revised for the term abroad. Meet the ILR study abroad advisor to check how transfer status counts.

schools.name: Notre Dame
schools.one: Pick a college and major, then get credit guidance from the military-connected admissions counselor.
facts: Lists 24 transferable credits.
Recent admitted transfers averaged a 3.75+ GPA.
schools.next: Choose the college and major. Send all prior college transcripts for credit and curriculum advice. Fall 2027 submission opens January 15.

fin.waiver: No transfer fee-waiver rule was found. Ask admissions.
fin.model: A VetLink guide lists Notre Dame as need-blind for all admitted students. An official statement for transfers was not found. Transfer students are not eligible for merit scholarships.
fin.aid: From your call: a household income of $60,000 or less covers tuition, fees, housing and food, and up to $150,000 covers at least full tuition. You do not have to use the GI Bill to attend. Fall transfer deadline March 15.
fin.vet: Yellow Ribbon school. On your call, a 100% GI Bill pays up to about $30,000 a year more or less. Service to School VetLink, Warrior-Scholar Project and a veterans law clinic.

schools.abroad: Students in approved programs count as enrolled at Notre Dame for federal aid. Aid is not guaranteed abroad, and non-Notre Dame programs need a Consortium Agreement. Because Notre Dame meets need, outside funds can adjust your aid. Same fees as campus plus a $750 study abroad fee. No rule specific to transfer entrants was found: ask Global Study Abroad.

schools.name: Yale
schools.one: Build recent liberal-arts and quantitative coursework, and confirm your current course record before following up.
facts: Needs two recommendation letters and every college and high-school transcript.
No admissions credit floor or ceiling, but degree credit is capped.
Meets demonstrated need; EWSP students are financially independent for aid.
schools.next: Strengthen recent English and math work, then follow up with an updated record. Consider whether a later cycle fits better.

fin.waiver: Automatic for U.S. veterans and active duty: answer Yes to the military fee waiver question in the Program Materials section.
fin.model: Yale admits without regard to ability to pay and meets 100% of demonstrated need for Eli Whitney students. EWSP students are treated as independent, so parental income is not counted.
fin.aid: Financial aid application due April 1. Materials due March 15 (one Yale page says March 18, so confirm).
fin.vet: Yellow Ribbon participant. Yale's veteran and military student office handles benefit coordination.

schools.abroad: Eli Whitney students can study abroad for a year or term with approval from the program director and the Committee on the Year or Term Abroad, doing full-time university-level work. Yale aid carries abroad with a budget form, capped at two terms. After returning you must enroll in Yale College: the catalog says two terms and a study abroad page says one, so confirm.

schools.name: Princeton
schools.one: Lock down a graded paper that qualifies, and confirm the one-year transferable-credit threshold.
facts: The graded paper is an academic course paper with its prompt, grade and any comments. Expository, thesis-driven writing is preferred.
Princeton posts these dates as subject to change.
schools.next: Ask the office for written guidance on transfer credit and on which recent course papers qualify. Plan the economics and statistics coursework.

fin.waiver: Automatic: choose the US military veterans and servicemembers fee waiver option on the application. Lower-income applicants who apply for aid also get a waiver.
fin.model: Aid is need-based and Princeton aims to meet 100% of need. A clear official statement of need-blind transfer admission was not retrieved. Princeton aid can supplement or replace veterans benefits.
fin.aid: Princeton uses its own Princeton Financial Aid Application (PFAA) and does not require or accept the CSS Profile or IDOC. Transfer aid deadline March 9.
fin.vet: Participates in Service to School VetLink, Warrior-Scholar Project and the Leadership Scholar Program. Yellow Ribbon coordination through financial aid.

schools.abroad: Study abroad is open to spring-term sophomores, juniors and fall-term seniors with a 3.0 or higher GPA the prior year, and most students go no earlier than spring of sophomore year. Princeton need-based aid carries to approved academic-year programs, but the Princeton Grant does not cover summer programs. Transfer-specific rules were not found: ask the Study Abroad Program.

schools.name: Tufts REAL
schools.one: Ask REAL how your credits count and whether you must study full-time.
facts: Financial-aid materials are due in mid-April 2027. The official page does not publish the exact day.
schools.next: Ask about credits, full-time study and recent coursework. Request an aid estimate.

fin.waiver: No automatic waiver is stated on the REAL page: contact REAL if the fee is a hardship. Tufts Engineering lists an $85 waiver for military and veterans, so confirm for REAL.
fin.model: Need-based aid for eligible REAL students, meeting 100% of demonstrated need. Need-blind status was not confirmed. File the Tufts Financial Aid Form as well as the FAFSA. If you do not apply for aid now, you are not eligible for institutional aid in later years.
fin.aid: Application due March 15, 2027. Aid materials are due mid-April, with the exact day unpublished. Say on the REAL application that you intend to use VA benefits.
fin.vet: Yellow Ribbon: $5,000 a year from Tufts, matched by the VA, for veterans at 100% Post-9/11 eligibility.

schools.abroad: Aid transfers automatically for Tufts-run programs. For external programs only federal and state aid and loans transfer, through a Consortium Agreement, and Tufts grants do not. Courses need department approval. Whether REAL students can use study abroad was not found: ask REAL.

schools.name: WashU
schools.one: Choose your undergraduate school, then confirm the major, credit path and aid.
facts: A portfolio is required only for College of Art or College of Architecture applicants.
St. Louis is a minor location plus.
schools.next: Pick the school and major, confirm credits and aid, and judge whether a visit is feasible.

fin.waiver: The $75 fee is waived for U.S. veterans applying for first-year or transfer admission: indicate eligibility on the Common App or Coalition App. It is also waived for applicants applying for need-based aid.
fin.model: International transfer applicants are not eligible for aid. Need-blind status for domestic transfers was not confirmed.
fin.aid: Application and aid working date March 1, 2027. Verify when WashU relabels the Fall 2027 calendar.
fin.vet: Yellow Ribbon was not confirmed in this search: ask financial aid.

schools.abroad: Need-based aid and scholarships can apply to approved WashU study abroad programs, but generally not to summer programs. A 3.0 GPA is required, and a C or better for credit. Transfer-specific rules were not found: ask Overseas Programs.

schools.name: Northwestern
schools.one: Verify the conflicting April aid dates before you rely on either one.
facts: The binding transfer plan conflicts with keeping Brown first, so use the regular route.
The admissions table lists aid on Apr 1. The aid office lists FAFSA and CSS Profile on Apr 15 and tax forms on Apr 20.
schools.next: Assess academic fit and credit transfer, then ask the aid office which aid date applies.
d: Regular application (admissions table also lists aid)
FAFSA and CSS Profile, aid office date
Federal tax forms, aid office date

fin.waiver: Armed Forces or Veteran Fee Waiver, plus hardship waivers, requested through a Common App or Coalition profile question. The fee is $75 otherwise. Requesting a waiver does not disadvantage you.
fin.model: Need-aware or need-blind status for transfers was not established. Verify with admissions.
fin.aid: FAFSA and CSS Profile are both required (Northwestern CSS code 1565). Your audited list shows April 1 for the application, April 15 for FAFSA and CSS, and April 20 for tax forms. A search result cited March 15 and the admissions table lists aid on April 1, so verify before relying on any date.
fin.vet: Yellow Ribbon was not confirmed in this search: ask the aid office.

schools.abroad: Study abroad eligibility starts the summer after you finish your first year at Northwestern, and this applies to transfers too, with a 2.5 GPA. Need-based aid covers Northwestern, exchange and partner programs but not independent programs. Summer aid covers one summer. Study abroad credit is treated as transfer credit.
links: School of Education and Social Policy

schools.name: Georgetown
schools.one: Pick your school and major, and check the four-full-semester ceiling.
facts: The Jan 15 priority date applies only to junior Public Policy or Environment and Sustainability routes.
First core school to swap out if the list stays too reach-heavy.
schools.next: Confirm the intended school and major and full-time semester eligibility. If applying as a junior to Public Policy or Environment and Sustainability, decide before January 15.
d: Junior Public Policy or Environment and Sustainability priority application

fin.waiver: Fee waiver requests are accepted from any applicant for whom the fee is a significant burden, using the NACAC or College Board form. The deadline does not move for waiver requests.
fin.model: Need-based aid only. Georgetown meets 100% of demonstrated need for U.S. citizens and permanent residents. International transfers are not eligible for aid.
fin.aid: Submit both the FAFSA and the CSS Profile. Application and aid March 1, with the junior Public Policy or Environment and Sustainability priority date January 15. Decisions by June 1.
fin.vet: Dossier lists Yellow Ribbon with a full tuition match in the College. Confirm on Georgetown's military and veterans page.

schools.abroad: All aid except Federal Work-Study applies to Georgetown-approved and independent petition study abroad programs, and students in Global Education programs stay matriculated. No study abroad while on probation. Summer aid needs 6 or more credits. Georgetown Qatar covers one semester. Transfer-specific rules were not found: ask the Office of Global Education.

schools.name: Vanderbilt
schools.one: Confirm where you would land academically, the four-semester residency and your aid plan.
facts: More transfer seats and a full-need policy for admitted transfers.
schools.next: Confirm the program, residence requirement and aid plan, and show recent full-time rigor.

fin.waiver: $50 application fee or a fee waiver for qualified students, through the Common App or Coalition transfer application. Vanderbilt issues no CSS fee-waiver codes: the CSS Profile may waive its own fee based on your answers.
fin.model: A secondary source says Vanderbilt meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted transfers. Verify on Vanderbilt's own site.
fin.aid: Your audited list shows February 1 for FAFSA and CSS priority and February 15 for the priority application.
fin.vet: The registrar certifies VA benefits. Yellow Ribbon contributions vary by school, so get a written estimate from the VA School Certifying Official.

schools.abroad: Transfer students can apply to study abroad after completing their first semester at Vanderbilt per the policies page, though another source says two semesters, so reconcile with the Study Abroad office. Semester and academic-year programs through Vanderbilt are eligible for federal and Vanderbilt aid, and the package can increase if a program costs more than a comparable term. Summer aid is limited.

schools.name: Williams
schools.one: Plan around the two-year residence rule: a junior-entry transfer must give up transfer credit to study away.
facts: Transfer credit is capped at two years of credit, and Williams requires two years in residence.
Offers only need-based aid, with no merit scholarships. The CSS Profile is required for non-federal aid.
Official dates conflict: the aid page lists March 3, the Common App March 2, an older catalog March 1.
schools.next: Confirm the March date on the official page, decide sophomore or junior entry, and ask the admission office how a veteran transfer is reviewed.
d: Application and financial aid (official page may list March 3)

fin.waiver: The $65 fee can be waived, and Williams says asking does not disadvantage you. Veterans can request a waiver on the Common App. The CSS Profile fee can also be waived, and the $200 enrollment deposit too.
fin.model: Williams offers only need-based aid with no merit scholarships. Need-blind status for transfers was not stated. The CSS Profile is required for non-federal aid.
fin.aid: Admission and aid applications are due together, with no extra materials for transfer aid. The official date is unclear (March 1 to 3).
fin.vet: Williams encourages veterans to apply, as first-year or transfer depending on college coursework. Service to School VetLink guidebook has a Williams page.

schools.abroad: Williams requires two years in residence and caps transfer credit at two years. A student who enrolls as a junior and wants to study away must give up a semester or year of transfer credit to meet residence. Aid recipients submit a budget proposal for study away. A new tuition model removes a $1,500 study away fee from the Class of 2029, except for Williams-Exeter and Williams-Mystic. Whether transfers can join Williams-Exeter was not stated.

schools.name: Wesleyan
schools.one: Apply for aid with the application: the fee is waived then, and skipping aid costs you aid eligibility for a year.
facts: Fall transfer applications are due March 15, with notification on May 15 (a Wesleyan aid page gives a conflicting late-April date).
Meets 100% of demonstrated need with loan-free packages, but is need-aware for transfer admission.
Applicants who say they will not seek aid are not eligible for Wesleyan aid until after one year enrolled.
schools.next: Confirm the Fall 2027 dates, file the aid request with the application, and ask how a veteran transfer is reviewed.
d: Application and financial aid request (confirm Fall 2027 date)

fin.waiver: The application fee is automatically waived for any student applying for financial aid.
fin.model: Meets 100% of demonstrated need with loan-free packages for domestic students, but is need-aware for transfer admission. International transfers get very limited aid.
fin.aid: Aid request due March 15. If you say you will not seek aid, you are not eligible for Wesleyan aid until after one year (two full semesters) enrolled.
fin.vet: Veterans benefits and Yellow Ribbon were not researched: ask financial aid.

schools.abroad: Semester and year study abroad for credit counts as Wesleyan enrollment, so Wesleyan tuition is charged and aid applies. The Office of Study Abroad prepares a budget sheet and aid is revised from it. Work-study is replaced by a grant. Wesleyan aid does not cover summer or winter programs. Transfer-specific rules were not found: ask the Office of Study Abroad.

schools.name: Amherst
schools.one: Send the transfer essay (250 to 500 words on your reasons for transferring) and confirm the Fall 2027 date.
facts: Transfer applicants submit the Common App or Coalition transfer application plus the Amherst supplement.
A Veteran Fee Waiver is listed on the Common App, and the fee can also be waived through Quick Pass.
No interview is required for admission consideration.
schools.next: Follow up after your admissions call, confirm the March date on the official page, and ask about transfer aid and study abroad.

fin.waiver: A $65 fee or a fee waiver request through the Common App, Coalition App or Quick Pass. The Common App lists a Veteran Fee Waiver.
fin.model: A secondary source says Amherst aims to meet 100% of demonstrated need for transfers and is need-blind for U.S. applicants. Amherst's own transfer aid page was not retrieved.
fin.aid: No transfer-specific aid deadlines could be verified. Confirm on the official page.
fin.vet: Dossier lists a veterans program with Posse Veterans and VetLink. Unverified: ask admissions.

schools.abroad: No official Amherst rule on study abroad or aid for transfer students was found. Ask admissions or the financial aid office.

schools.name: USC Iovine and Young
schools.one: Calculate the 3 to 4 year time and cost, and verify MATH 118 or 125 equivalency, before investing.
facts: USC overall transfer rate was 26.1% in the Fall 2026 profile, with admitted GPAs of 3.70 to 3.97. Those are not Academy figures.
Academy essays go in SlideRoom, with up to four optional portfolio pieces.
schools.next: Work out the realistic finish date and aid. If you apply, submit the required Academy essays and choose optional portfolio items.

fin.waiver: Veteran or service member waiver: select it under the school-specific question in the USC Questions section of the Common App. Hardship waivers are also available.
fin.model: USC describes itself as need-blind for admission. Veterans should file the FAFSA and CSS Profile even when planning to use VA benefits, and can choose the GI Bill after seeing the aid package.
fin.aid: Your audited list shows February 15 for the application and March 2 for FAFSA and CSS priority filing. Other USC pages cite earlier dates, so verify.
fin.vet: Yellow Ribbon participant with an unlimited undergraduate program for eligible students. USC says eligible undergraduates with remaining GI Bill can graduate debt-free.

schools.abroad: Iovine and Young BS students can fulfil up to 12 major units abroad with faculty approval, limited to major electives, with spring of junior year preferred. Whether aid applies to an Academy study abroad term was not found: ask. Outside-transfer eligibility for the Academy also needs written confirmation.
links: Why USC does not track interest

schools.name: SMU
schools.one: Apply only if a scholarship plus benefits makes SMU close to free. Get a written net-cost estimate first.
facts: The admission-balance option: 1,190 of 1,542 Fall 2025 transfer applicants were admitted (77.2%).
Automatic transfer merit consideration starts at a 3.3 GPA.
schools.next: Confirm major and credit fit, campus enjoyment and an actual aid estimate.
d: FAFSA and CSS Profile priority for fall transfer
schools.gate: Stays on the list only with a full, decent scholarship. Automatic transfer merit needs 24 transferable hours and a 3.3 GPA, and the larger awards need 3.5 or higher.

fin.waiver: The veterans page says SMU automatically waives the application fee for all undergraduate U.S. military veteran applicants. A newer sheet says all undergraduates this cycle, so confirm.
fin.model: Merit comes automatically with 24 transferable hours and a 3.30 GPA: the Founders Scholarship is $15,000 a year for up to six terms, the Transfer Honor Scholarship is half tuition at 3.5, and a full-tuition-and-fees award needs 3.7 (North Texas community college students). Your gate is a full, decent scholarship.
fin.aid: FAFSA and CSS priority February 1. Priority application April 1. Final application August 1.
fin.vet: Yellow Ribbon guarantees a 100% tuition benefit for eligible Post-9/11 veterans for the length of their entitlement. Veterans apply as transfer students.
fin.note: Ask for a written net-cost estimate, with scholarship and benefits combined, before applying.

schools.abroad: No transfer-specific study abroad award was found. Study abroad appears as an add-on in some first-year awards only.

bench.name: Duke
bench.one: Revisit if recent grades get substantially stronger.
facts: 2025-26: 160 transfer admits from 2,460 applicants.

bench.name: Rice
bench.one: Revisit with a verified current record.
facts: Recent-college GPA minimum of 3.2; admitted transfers are typically 3.5+.

bench.name: UChicago
bench.one: Check the current transfer cohort and curricular fit before adding.
facts: Not yet researched against the current cycle.

bench.name: Columbia GS
bench.one: Only with a verified financing plan.
facts: GS says it cannot meet every student's full financial need.

brown.diText: Brown publishes no transfer interest score. The binding rolling option is a contractual commitment, not a signal.
brown.path: A policy-oriented concentration, Africana Studies, Science, Technology and Society, or Modern Culture and Media. Not computer science first. On your call Brown noted that a concentration is like a major with its own requirements, and that even a policy concentration can carry a math requirement, so statistics helps. Confirm the exact concentration.
know: Suresh Venkatasubramanian
Directs the Center for Technological Responsibility, Reimagination and Redesign (CNTR): technology and policy lane.
Harini Suresh
Sociotechnical dimensions of AI, fairness and how affected communities experience automated systems.
brown.res: CNTR and the Socially Responsible Computing program
brown.evi: Since 2019, trained Socially Responsible Computing teaching assistants work inside technical courses. CNTR and the CS program built a public handbook of teachable primers, and the 2025-26 teams spanned CS, public policy, graphic design, philosophy and STS.
brown.who: Becky (Veterans admissions, call held). Brown is a Service to School VetLink partner.
brown.ask: How have project-based courses typically mapped into Brown credit, and what sequencing would remain for a policy, Africana Studies or STS concentration?
brown.show: One finished project plus one unresolved question. Use the optional 90-second video for voice, not a résumé recap. Include the JST, résumé and VetLink Addendum.
brown.dont: Do not submit the Common App or RUE in parallel. Do not cold-email the CNTR director.

cornell.diText: Cornell publishes no transfer interest factor. Choosing the right college and finishing its prerequisites matter far more.
cornell.path: ILR BS: labor, technology, workplace systems, policy and economics. Africana Studies is available as a minor, and as a transfer you cannot double major across two Cornell colleges (Kyle, call). The earlier faculty research was written for Information Science, so treat it as method context until ILR faculty are researched.
know: Claire Cardie
Natural-language processing, argumentation and human-centered NLP.
Allison Koenecke
Algorithmic fairness, including automated systems in public benefits and health.
René Kizilcec
Directs the Future of Learning Lab; education technology and computational social science.
cornell.evi: A field study of 1.4 million registrations across 159 online courses at 20 institutions found that course discipline, stated prerequisites and gender cues predicted who enrolled, while instructor skin color, diversity references and description style did not show the expected effects.
cornell.who: Kyle (admissions, call held), ILR transfer admissions, and the Cornell veterans admissions ambassador.
cornell.ask: Please evaluate these exact course titles, descriptions and grades for ILR sophomore or junior entry.
cornell.show: One finished project with its human consequences, tied to a specific Cornell method. The required recommendation comes from a college instructor who graded substantial work.
cornell.dont: Do not mass-contact faculty or mail packages. Name a professor only after reading one current project or paper.

nd.diText: Notre Dame says it does not track prospective-student interest. What counts is prerequisites at B or higher, college performance, a specific transfer statement and space in the major.
nd.path: College of Arts and Letters with Africana Studies as the likely major, plus the cross-college Tech Ethics minor. Law school is the long-term aim, and the veterans law clinic came up on your call. The IDEA Center is a resource, not a degree.
know: Mohammad Rashidujjaman Rifat
HCI; AI ethics and cultural and value pluralism.
Nitesh Chawla
Founding director of the Lucy Family Institute for Data and Society.
Meghan Sullivan
Director of the Institute for Ethics and the Common Good.
nd.evi: The BenchmarkCards project standardized documentation of LLM benchmark properties, bias and evaluation methods, with a public benchmark database. The Ethical Cities program pairs students and faculty with South Bend organizations.
nd.who: Montanna Kirven (veteran liaison) or the Office of Military and Veterans Affairs. Michael (call held).
nd.ask: How will the 24-credit threshold and Arts and Letters prerequisites treat my quarter-based SCAD Applied AI studios?
nd.show: A PDF syllabus for every post-high-school course, named exactly by course number. A transfer statement built on technology ethics and the common good. The optional 60 to 90 second Glimpse video only if it adds voice.
nd.dont: Do not ask the liaison, a professor or an alumnus for a recommendation. Do not mail extras.

yale.diText: Yale states that it does not track event registration or contact with admissions staff.
yale.path: Ethnicity, Race and Migration through Eli Whitney is the pick in your notes. Computing and the Arts and African American Studies also appear in your research. Confirm the order.
know: Marynel Vázquez
Human-robot interaction and social AI.
Theodore Kim
Computer graphics and the Critical Computing Initiative.
yale.evi: The group traced bias in rendering back to data, physical assumptions and algorithms. Its 2023 "Lifted Curls" model for tightly coiled hair won best paper at the Symposium on Computer Animation.
yale.who: The Eli Whitney (EWSP) office, Patricia Wei (call held), and the Yale veteran and military student office.
yale.ask: Given my exact timeline, should I use EWSP rather than conventional transfer, and how are studio computing courses evaluated toward Computing and the Arts?
yale.show: One strong graded analytical paper, recent coursework across writing, quantitative reasoning, humanities and science, and a focused academic statement. Prepare for a possible interview.
yale.dont: Do not mail creative packages, lobby after no interview, or ask faculty to advocate.

princeton.diText: Princeton says explicitly that it does not track demonstrated interest and that attending an information session does not affect admission.
princeton.path: Top three on your list: Operations Research and Financial Engineering (ORFE), African American Studies and Computer Science. Your notes name African American Studies as the Princeton pick. The overview you prepared for Alex Bustin points to a BSE in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, so settle the final order before the essays.
know: Ruha Benjamin
African American Studies; science, technology and social inequity.
Arvind Narayanan
Directs the Center for Information Technology Policy (technology and policy lane).
Olga Russakovsky
Visual AI Lab: human-centered AI and fairness (Computer Science lane).
princeton.res: H-ARC, a public human abstraction and reasoning dataset
princeton.evi: Solution attempts from more than 1,700 people on all 800 original ARC tasks, published with action traces and natural-language rule descriptions, so abstraction can be studied beyond accuracy.
princeton.who: Alex Bustin (military admissions, meeting held), Keith Shaw (transfer and veteran program), Silvia Rodriguez (veteran financial aid).
princeton.ask: How are my courses evaluated toward distribution and the prerequisites for ORFE or African American Studies, and which graded paper best shows readiness?
princeton.show: The graded paper with its prompt, grade and instructor comments, and two academic recommenders including one college instructor. Show the preparation each lane expects, such as quantitative coursework for ORFE. The arts supplement only if the work truly fits.
princeton.dont: Do not send physical portfolios outside the arts supplement, mass-email professors or ask an alumnus to endorse.
princeton.gap: ORFE faculty and research are not yet researched. Add one current ORFE paper or project.

tufts.diText: Tufts says it records legitimate engagement such as official visits, email or phone contact and virtual events. No REAL-specific weight is published. The supplement asks how you have engaged with Tufts, so only true engagement counts.
tufts.path: Arts and Sciences social-science or cognitive path: sociology, Science, Technology and Society, cognitive and brain science or economics. Computer science appears only as coursework, not the major. SMFA studio work needs written confirmation from REAL and SMFA.
know: Elaine Schaertl Short
Disability-centered, human-in-the-loop machine learning and assistive robotics.
Matthias Scheutz
Directs human-robot interaction research; robot ethics.
tufts.res: HCI Lab fNIRS mental-workload dataset and the public STS Lunch Seminar
tufts.evi: Brain-activity recordings from 87 participants during n-back tasks at four workload levels (68 meet the quality threshold), released with code under CC BY 4.0 to study interfaces that adapt to mental workload.
tufts.ask: Which syllabi should I supply to separate credit for my intended Arts and Sciences major from general electives, and can REAL students use SMFA studio courses?
tufts.show: Two recent-instructor recommendations, an Applied AI case study and a credit worksheet. Complete at least two genuine engagement steps: a REAL information session and one direct question.
tufts.dont: Do not submit both REAL and conventional transfer. Do not claim a visit, event or conversation that did not happen.

washu.diText: WashU announced it will consider demonstrated interest for Fall 2027 high-school applicants. It has not said this applies to transfers. Ask once and give attendance no weight until it answers.
washu.path: Arts and Sciences: Sociology, Philosophy-Neuroscience-Psychology, or anthropology with digital humanities. Sam Fox (Design) only with a portfolio. Not computer science. A new 15-credit computational AI minor is open across schools.
know: Alvitta Ottley
Adaptive visualization, decision-making and human-computer interaction.
Gabi Kirilloff
Digital humanities; computational methods for literature and culture.
washu.evi: Uses computational stylometry and interpretation to test how generative models imitate nineteenth-century literary style. The Digital Transformation Research Corps also runs St. Louis cultural-asset mapping.
washu.ask: Does the Fall 2027 demonstrated-interest policy apply to transfer applicants, and how will my SCAD quarter courses convert?
washu.show: The instructor evaluation and College Report. A portfolio is required only for College of Art or Architecture applicants. A short research note on AI Style or a St. Louis project, where it explains real fit.
washu.dont: Do not cold-contact faculty for admission guidance.

nu.diText: Northwestern publishes no interest scoring for regular transfer. Its binding Transfer Early Decision (TED) is the one legitimate signal, and it conflicts with keeping Brown first.
nu.path: Not Computer Science. Your target major is not recorded yet. Candidates close to your ILR and Peabody interest are the School of Education and Social Policy (Learning and Organizational Change, Social Policy) and Weinberg (Sociology, African American Studies). Confirm the exact names with Northwestern before choosing.
know: Elizabeth Gerber
Co-directs the Center for Human-Computer Interaction + Design. A cross-school anchor, not a degree path.
Nicholas Diakopoulos
Directs the Computational Journalism Lab; algorithmic accountability. A cross-school anchor.
nu.evi: Links design, learning sciences, communication, computing, psychology and social behavior, and runs public Thought Leader Dialogues that anyone can follow.
nu.ask: Which School of Education and Social Policy or Weinberg major fits a veteran transfer interested in people, organizations and policy, and how do my credits map?
nu.show: A school-specific reason that names a real major and cites cross-school pathways accurately.
nu.dont: Do not cold-email Gerber or Diakopoulos for admissions help.
nu.gap: Faculty for the School of Education and Social Policy and Weinberg paths are not yet researched.

gt.diText: Georgetown publishes no transfer interest scoring. School-specific knowledge belongs in the supplement.
gt.path: BS in Science, Technology and International Affairs (STIA) in the School of Foreign Service. The Beeck Center is a center, not a degree.
know: Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation
A resource to cite carefully. It is not an academic program.
gt.res: Beeck Center for Social Impact and Innovation
gt.gap: No research-library brief exists for Georgetown yet. Read one current Beeck or STIA project and record what it found.
gt.ask: How should I sequence the recommended economics, statistics or calculus and language preparation for STIA, and how many full-time semesters can I still count?
gt.show: Aligned coursework (B+ or higher is recommended) and a supplement that shows real knowledge of STIA.
gt.dont: Confirm the maximum prior full-time enrollment rule in writing before investing heavily.

vandy.diText: Vanderbilt marks interest not considered in its first-year data and gives transfer applicants no basis for interest points. One concise curricular question is enough.
vandy.path: Peabody College: Human and Organizational Development (HOD), your ILR equivalent. Not computer science.
know: Jenny L. Davis
Sociology; the politics and ethics of technological design. A cross-college anchor, not an HOD faculty member.
vandy.res: Vanderbilt Smart Cities work with Nashville
vandy.evi: Transit tools built with WeGo, and a 2022 NSF Civic Innovation Challenge project exploring an AI-supported system that routes appropriate non-emergency incidents away from emergency response.
vandy.who: Your assigned admissions counselor (use the official lookup), admissions@vanderbilt.edu, 615-322-2561. The VA School Certifying Official handles benefits.
vandy.ask: How would my courses be evaluated for Peabody HOD, and what syllabus evidence helps the evaluator?
vandy.show: Two instructor recommendations, at least one from a college instructor. A theme of how people, organizations and systems work or fail, with the Nashville emergency-routing project as a civic example.
vandy.dont: Do not ask an alumnus, adviser or professor for a letter. Do not mail an interest letter.
vandy.gap: HOD faculty and research are not yet researched.

williams.diText: No published transfer interest rule was found. Ask once.
williams.path: Majors on file are Africana Studies and Cognitive Science (older dossier). Your target is not recorded yet. Confirm it.
williams.gap: Not researched in the library yet. Add one Williams department, course or project you have read.
williams.who: Williams admission office. The Service to School VetLink guidebook has a Williams page.
williams.ask: How does Williams review a veteran transfer with SCAD and prior college credit, and does the two-year residence rule change my entry year?
williams.show: A school-specific reason that names a real department and shows tested fit.
williams.dont: Do not send extras or contact faculty for admissions help.

wesleyan.diText: No interest policy has been researched yet. Ask once.
wesleyan.path: No major is on file for Wesleyan, and your notes do not cover it. Name the one you want.
wesleyan.gap: Not researched in the library or your notes. Add one department, course or project you have read.
wesleyan.ask: Given need-aware transfer admission, how does applying for aid affect review, and how are veteran transfers evaluated?
wesleyan.show: A school-specific reason that names a real major.
wesleyan.dont: Do not skip the aid request to look stronger: it limits aid for a year.

amherst.diText: No interest policy has been researched yet. Ask once.
amherst.path: Black Studies and the Open Curriculum are on file (older dossier). Your target is not recorded yet. Confirm it.
amherst.gap: Not researched in the library yet. Add one Amherst course or project you have read.
amherst.ask: How does the Open Curriculum handle transfer credit, and what aid does Amherst offer a veteran transfer?
amherst.show: A transfer essay that names the real reason for moving and a specific Amherst fit.

usc.diText: USC states directly that it does not track demonstrated interest. Event attendance and emails add no points.
usc.path: Iovine and Young Academy BS. Dornsife BA Cognitive Science and Annenberg are the liberal-arts alternates. The sequential curriculum can mean 3 to 4 years.
know: Kate Crawford
Annenberg; the power, labor and politics of AI; Anatomy of an AI System.
Bistra Dilkina
Co-directs the Center for AI in Society.
usc.evi: An AI-assisted network intervention with youth experiencing homelessness reported a 40% increase in HIV testing. A three-year collaboration with the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority and UCLA's California Policy Lab identified racial bias in housing triage and developed fairer decision support.
usc.who: Iovine and Young admissions: iyaadmission@usc.edu (one email with a one-page course list). The Veterans Resource Center handles transition and benefits.
usc.ask: Which Academy requirements are non-waivable for an external transfer, and should I budget three or four USC years?
usc.show: Required Academy essays in SlideRoom and up to four optional portfolio items. Lead with one case study covering problem framing, research, prototype, testing and what was learned.
usc.dont: Do not ask faculty for a pre-review or recommendation. Do not mail a creative package.

smu.diText: SMU's first-year data considers interest, and no transfer factor is published. One precise question helps you plan. It earns no points.
smu.path: Meadows BA in Creative Computing is the closest fit but leans toward computing. Film and Media Arts or Public Relations and Strategic Communication are the alternates in your plan.
know: Ira Greenberg
Creative coding, data visualization and agentic or LLM systems.
Corey Clark
Gaming technology, AI and societal challenges at the Guildhall.
smu.res: Intelligent Systems and Bias Examination Lab (ISaBEL)
smu.evi: Generated more than one million diverse synthetic facial images to study demographic bias in facial recognition. The "Dark Shadows" game helps organize real human-trafficking information from Department of Justice releases while protecting victim identity.
smu.who: Your assigned transfer counselor: transfer@smu.edu, 214-768-2058. MilVets supports military-connected students.
smu.ask: Can SCAD Applied AI, creative coding, UX and computing courses satisfy Creative Computing requirements, or do they enter as electives?
smu.show: Two to four portfolio works with role, method, result and reflection, sent only if requested. Use the April 1 priority date for scholarship consideration.
smu.dont: Do not send physical materials or cold-message faculty. Give SMU the same seriousness as a reach.
